data.title: Yes Bank’s CET1 ratio to take 250-basis-point hit after AT1 bond ruling
data.description:
Following the Supreme Court upholding the 2023 Bombay High Court judgment quashing the write-down of Additional Tier (AT)-1 Bonds aggregating ₹8,415 crore by Yes Bank, the Bank said the pro forma impact of reinstatement of these Bonds’ principal amount on Common Equity Tier (CET) 1 Ratio (including profits) as on June 30, 2026 is expected to be 250 basis points.

However, the Tier-1 Ratio on a pro forma basis will remain unchanged at 14 per cent.

In a regulatory filing, the Bank said it is examining the Supreme Court judgment in detail, including evaluating all available legal options and suitable actions/steps going forward.

Yes Bank emphasised that it has access to appropriate capital-management levers and can undertake additional capital actions, as it deems appropriate, to pursue its growth objectives.

S&P says Yes Bank can withstand capital impact

S&P Global Ratings assessed that Yes Bank‘s credit profile can withstand the Supreme Court of India’s ruling that the write-off of its additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds was illegal.

The agency underscored that Yes Bank’s regulatory capital is adequate. As of the end of March 2026, the bank’s CET1 ratio stood at a healthy 13.87%, providing a significant cushion. It said. This will allow the bank to absorb an anticipated 250 basis-point impact on its CET1 while remaining well above the minimum regulatory requirement of 5.5%

“In our view, this ruling relates to procedures that Yes Bank did not follow under the reconstruction scheme exercised during the 2020 rescue. The Supreme Court decision is seen as addressing the procedural lapses in the write-down process rather than questioning the instrument’s fundamental loss-absorbing characteristics,” the rating agency said.

S&P noted that “it is unclear whether Yes Bank will challenge the ruling, however, if enforced, we do not expect it to affect our ratings on the bank.”

AT1 bonds are designed to absorb losses

Under the Basel III framework, AT1 instruments are specifically designed to absorb losses through either conversion into common equity or a write-down mechanism once a pre-specified trigger point is met.

In India, this trigger typically occurs when the common equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio falls below 6.125% of risk-weighted assets, or when regulators determine the issuer is no longer viable.

Capital ratios expected to remain adequate

S&P expects Yes Bank to remain adequately capitalised, with its risk-adjusted capital (RAC) ratio projected to stay within the 8.0%-8.5% range through the fiscal years ending March 31, 2027 and 2028, compared with 9.0% as of March 2026.

“We do not anticipate any meaningful impact on our total adjusted capital (the numerator for our RAC ratio calculation). We expect the negative impact of approximately Indian rupee (INR) 84 billion (Rs 8,400 crore) to common equity to be largely offset by the reinstatement of the AT1 instruments to a similar extent. Going forward, we see this as earnings negative as the AT1’s has high coupon payments of 9.0%-9.5%,” the agency said.

Coupon payments remain a key uncertainty

The Supreme Court order states that the coupon rate will remain unaffected by the outcome of the appeals and must be made in terms of the information memoranda.

“Like other AT1s, Yes Bank’s AT1 also allows for discretionary coupon payments; however, it is unclear if the bank will pay coupons for the 5.5-year intervening period. We note that Dhanalaxmi Bank Ltd. was permitted to defer coupon payments on its Basel II-compliant Tier II instruments, demonstrating the loss-absorption potential of such hybrid debt.

“We currently do not expect material impact of this on the bank’s credit profile but will continue to monitor any related developments. Yes Bank last paid a dividend on its common equity in 2019,” S&P said.

data.title: Canada, India aim to conclude CEPA by year-end; Fairfax deal signals investment momentum
data.description:
India and Canada are on track to conclude negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of this year, with the next round of talks scheduled for the week of November 9 in India, Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu said on Friday.

“We've completed five rounds. We're going to be doing another round on the week of November 9 back here in India,” Sidhu said at a press conference in Bengaluru, as Canada concluded its largest trade mission to India in three decades.

Pointing to Fairfax Financial Holdings’ acquisition of a majority stake in IDBI Bank in a deal valued at nearly C$8 billion, Sidhu said the transaction reflected growing investor confidence in India and could encourage further investment. He noted that Fairfax had already invested significantly in India, including in Bengaluru International Airport.

The deal, he said, sent a “clear signal to the supply chains that Canada is ready to do more”.

Expand exposure

Canadian pension funds and large institutions have collectively invested close to C$107 billion in India across sectors including roads, highways, healthcare, technology, clean technology and energy, Sidhu said, adding that investors were looking to expand their exposure.

The trade mission brought 300 business delegates representing 150 organisations to India. More than 30 deals between Canadian delegates and Indian partners, valued at nearly C$300 million, were recorded during the visit, he said.

The sectors represented opportunities for deeper collaboration in energy, critical minerals, fertilisers, aerospace, artificial intelligence, quantum computing and data centres. Sidhu said Canadian fertiliser exports to India had grown 85 per cent over recent years, while aerospace exports rose 300 per cent last year.

The two countries are seeking to more than double bilateral trade to C$70 billion by 2030, with the proposed CEPA expected to improve market access for businesses on both sides.

data.title: Ola Electric’s ₹1,000 crore rights issue uncovers SEBI scrutiny, audit deficiencies
data.description:
Ola Electric is seeking nearly ₹1,000 crore from shareholders even as the electric two-wheeler maker and its founder, Bhavish Aggarwal, face a pending SEBI proceeding over allegedly misleading public disclosures. The company’s rights offer also reveals that auditors flagged the absence of mandatory internal audit systems at the company and two subsidiaries during FY26.

Against this backdrop, Aggarwal recently announced another distribution push.

“What energy our dealers have! First 150 onboarded, and it was amazing to host and interact with them in our factory!” he said in a social media communication reproduced in Ola’s October 9 stock exchange filing. The announcement did not specify how many dealer outlets were operational or their servicing capabilities.

Seeds of doubts

Kranthi Bathini, Director – Equity Strategy at WealthMills Securities, said the company’s statements and regulatory disclosures had created doubts among investors about the credibility of management communications, leaving them uncertain about what to believe or trust when management makes public announcements.

The concerns assume significance because Ola’s earlier network claims are under regulatory scrutiny. The offer document records a January 7, 2025, SEBI administrative warning after Aggarwal announced a fourfold expansion of company-owned stores on social media before informing the stock exchanges. The latest dealer communication, however, was disclosed to the bourses.

Orders or sales?

SEBI’s April 10 show-cause notice concerns Ola’s February 2025 announcement that it had sold more than 25,000 electric vehicles during the month.

According to the offer document, SEBI alleged that “the disclosed figure represented confirmed orders rather than completed sales involving registration and delivery”. It also questioned disclosures concerning payments, cancellations and fulfilment, alleging that only a portion translated into registrations and recognised revenue.

Ola subsequently clarified that the figure referred to bookings rather than recorded sales.

In Risk Factor 53, the company states: “We track certain operational metrics with internal systems and tools and do not independently verify such metrics.” These include sales volumes, order fulfilment and after-sales service volumes. Ola maintains that its reported metrics are accurate.

Disclosures questioned

SEBI’s notice also alleges misleading December 2024 announcements about more than 3,200 stores being co-located with service centres and an expansion to 4,000 stores. The regulator alleged that these disclosures contributed to an 8.45 per cent increase in Ola’s share price on December 2, 2024.

The notice further questions Roadster and Roadster X motorcycle prototype approvals and delivery timelines.

The offer document states that SEBI alleged Aggarwal “disseminated or was responsible for misleading public statements and corporate announcements and incorrectly certified matters relating to financial reporting and internal controls”.

Ola and Aggarwal filed a settlement application on June 8, 2026. It remained pending as of October 7. The allegations have not been established through a final regulatory order.

Control gaps

Separately, auditors reported that Ola Electric Mobility, Ola Cell Technologies and Ola Electric Technologies lacked mandatory internal audit systems during FY26. The consolidated internal financial controls report also contained a qualified opinion concerning inventory-verification controls at a subsidiary.

The ₹999.74-crore rights issue follows Ola’s ₹5,500-crore IPO in 2024 and ₹780.24-crore institutional placement in June 2026. The offer acknowledges that proceeds from earlier issues remain partly unutilised, while the latest fundraising covers overlapping purposes, including debt repayment, organic growth and general corporate expenditure.

Priced at ₹27 a share, the issue has an October 13 record date and runs from October 22 to 30. Aggarwal has pledged shares representing 4.32 per cent of Ola’s equity to finance his participation, according to the filing.

data.title: Tractor retail sales rise 13.7% YoY in September on low base effect
data.description:
India’s tractor retail sales rose 13.7 per cent year-on-year in September 2026 to 76,906 units from 67,612 units a year earlier with the relatively lower base of September 2025 given the implementation of GST 2.0, according to data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA).

Tractor sales in September 2026, however, declined 12.6 per cent month-on-month amid a late festive calendar and patchy monsoon conditions.

Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and its Swaraj division together accounting for nearly 42 per cent of the market, as per FADA data.

Most key manufacturers reported YoY growth in September with International Tractors Ltdreported the highest growth with 27.1 per cent.

The year-on-year growth in September needs to be interpreted with caution, as last year’s base was influenced by buyers postponing purchases ahead of the GST rate reduction, Poonam Upadhyay, Director, Crisil Ratings, said.

“The September [MoM] dip in tractor retail sales appears more a matter of timing than shift in underlying demand. Unlike most automobile segments, over 80 per cent of tractor sales are linked to rural markets, where purchase decisions are often aligned with auspicious periods and harvest-linked cash flows,” she said. With the festive season shifting into October this year, part of September demand appears to have been deferred, she added.

Escorts Kubota Limited Agri Machinery Business said that looking ahead, festive demand, crop harvesting and improving rural liquidity are expected to support industry volumes. However, the high base effect may continue to moderate industry growth in the near term.

data.title: Urban Company net loss widens in Q2, revenue up 41.4%
data.description:
Home services platform, Urban Company Ltd widened its consolidated net loss to ₹182.48 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to ₹59.33 crore in the year-ago period as it continued aggressive investments in InstaHelp. Consolidated revenue from operations grew 41.4 per cent to ₹537.29 crore. The company’s board also approved raising up to ₹2,500 crore through the issue of equity shares or other convertible securities via qualified institutional placement (QIP), subject to shareholder approval.

In the shareholders’ letter, the company’s management said, “Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter for Urban Company with continued growth momentum and margin expansion for our core business. At the same time, we continued to invest aggressively in InstaHelp, where unit economics improved despite rapid scale-up.”

On a consolidated basis, net transaction value (NTV) grew 39 per cent y-o-y to ₹1,432 crore. Orders delivered reached 15.1 million, up 103 per cent y-o-y, and annual transacting users reached nearly 10 million, up 35 per cent y-o-y it added.

On the proposed fundraise, the company said, “We are on track to achieve our targets, and are raising capital for strategic flexibility. We closed the quarter with ₹1,901 crore in cash and treasury investment. The business is materially larger than at listing, growth has stepped up, and we now operate three businesses at scale with proven economics.”

‘On track’

“The proposed raise of up to ₹2,500 crore is about flexibility: it lets us invest with conviction across each of them, cement leadership in InstaHelp, and pursue inorganic opportunities selectively, without trading off one for another. We remain on track for adjusted EBITDA break-even by Q3 FY28 and Adjusted EBITDA of ₹1,000 crore by FY31,” it added in its filing.

Revenue from India consumer services business, excluding InstaHelp, rose 28.4 per cent to ₹336.38 crore.

The company’s InstaHelp business, which offers households daily cleaning and housekeeping needs, reported a segment loss of ₹173.12 crore in the quarter, compared with ₹42.91 crore loss a year ago, according to the filing. The segment revenue rose to ₹20.54 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹1.43 crore in Q2 FY26. Net order value (NOV) declined from ₹138 to ₹114 on competitive intensity and introductory pricing for new users. “InstaHelp’s value to the platform extends beyond its own P&L: it is our highest-frequency offering and a meaningful source of new users for our core services. In this phase of category development we are prioritising market leadership. We expect losses to remain elevated for a few more quarters before they begin to come down,” it added.

data.title: SC verdict on YES Bank AT1 bonds brings relief for mutual funds, retail investors
data.description:
Nearly six years after many investors had written off any hope of recovery, the Supreme Court’s verdict on YES Bank’s ₹8,415 crore additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds has come as a major relief for mutual funds, financial institutions and retail investors.

The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the Bombay High Court’s 2023 order that had quashed the decision of the YES Bank administrator to write down the AT1 bonds during the bank’s reconstruction in 2020. With recovery now appearing increasingly likely, mutual funds are moving swiftly to safeguard the interests of investors who were holding units in schemes exposed to the bonds at the time of the write-down.

Nippon India Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, which had marked down their AT1 bond holdings to zero, have temporarily halted fresh subscriptions in certain debt schemes that still hold exposure to the securities. The move is aimed at preventing new investors from benefiting from a potential windfall that rightfully belongs to existing unitholders.

“We were holding YES Bank AT1 bonds in the Nippon India Retirement Fund Wealth Creation Scheme, which was not segregated and was valued at nil after the RBI had passed an order to write them off,” Nippon India Mutual Fund said.

“We await further details on the operationalisation of the order as the valuation aspect remains unclear,” it added.

Kotak Mahindra AMC has taken a similar approach in dealing with the unexpected recovery from the AT1 bonds. Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund had exposure of about ₹2,680 crore to the bonds, while Nippon India Mutual Fund’s exposure stood at around ₹2,150 crore.

Debt schemes

In contrast, Franklin Templeton had adopted a different approach when the crisis unfolded in March 2020. The fund house, which had exposure of about ₹590 crore to the bonds across three debt schemes, created a segregated portfolio on March 6, 2020, and issued separate units to investors who held the schemes on that date.

“Any amounts realised from these bonds will be distributed to unit-holders of the respective segregated portfolios in proportion to their holdings,” Franklin Templeton said.

According to Aakanksha Shukla, AVP-Wealth Management at Master Capital Services, investors who entered the schemes after the write-down should not be entitled to the recovery proceeds. However, without restrictions, they could potentially benefit from the recovery, which explains why some fund houses have suspended fresh subscriptions.

“The distribution of proceeds will be easier for debt funds that ring-fenced the troubled bonds through a segregated portfolio,” she said.

Apart from mutual funds, several institutional investors also stand to gain from the ruling. Sammaan Capital expects to recover about ₹662 crore, while 63 Moons Technologies could recover nearly ₹300 crore.

Relief for investors

The ruling has also brought relief to retail investors. Around 1,346 retail investors held AT1 bonds worth about ₹679 crore. Of these, 1,311 were existing YES Bank customers, including retired employees, senior citizens and homemakers, with investments aggregating around ₹663 crore.

“The Supreme Court verdict is an eye-opener for regulators that they cannot wriggle out of their responsibilities simply by writing off a problem that should have been identified at a much earlier stage,” said Kuldip Singh, a retired bank executive who invested in the AT1 bonds in 2020.

The AT1 bonds, which offered a coupon of 9-9.5 per cent and required a minimum investment of ₹1 crore, had attracted investors seeking a steady annual income. Following the Supreme Court’s ruling, many of them may finally see a recovery from an investment they had long considered lost.

data.title: Jio Platforms IPO: Ambani taps massive Reliance workforce to boost offering
data.description:
Billionaire Mukesh Ambani is looking to activate the vast workforce of Reliance Industries Ltd to drum up interest in the blockbuster initial public offering of his empire’s telecom and digital services arm Jio Platforms Ltd, even bringing forward some salaries to give employees access to investable cash.

The conglomerate has reached out to most of its nearly 420,000 employees across all group companies, encouraging them to consider investing in the $3.2 billion IPO, according to people familiar with the matter. Reliance released October salaries about 15 days earlier than usual, which gives workers access to funds, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. Staff were not told a reason for the early salary release.

Big push

The effort shows Ambani pulling out all the stops to make sure the listing, which is on track to become the biggest ever in India, is a success. For a group that has spent years turning Jio into one of India’s largest digital businesses, the IPO is also an opportunity to turn hundreds of thousands of employees — and potentially their families — into shareholders.

data.title: Kothari Industrial gets DGCA certification for KOAIR-10L agricultural spraying drone
data.description:
Kothari Industrial Corporation Ltd (KICL), the flagship company of the D.C. Kothari group, has secured a Type certification from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) for its KOAIR-10L agricultural spraying drone.

KOAIR-10L is a medium-class hexacopter designed for agrochemical spraying applications. It features a 10-litre spray tank with flat-fan nozzles for uniform application of pesticides, fertilisers, and plant nutrients.

Certification clears way for commercial rollout

With this certification, KICL can now proceed with commercial manufacturing, sale, and deployment of these drones across India,, subject to applicable regulatory requirements,, with each unit accompanied by a certificate of conformity.

The Type Certificate was granted under the applicable Certification Scheme for Unmanned Aircraft Systems and the Drone Rules, 2021, following technical evaluation and recommendation by TQ Cert Services, an authorised certification body.

Company highlights focus on smarter farming

“The Make in India initiative relies heavily on the agriculture sector. Keeping these in mind, we ventured into agri-drone technology with the concept of giving back to society, especially to the farming fraternity. We felt it would be the need of the hour — to make farming smarter and safer, cost-effective, a lifesaver for farmers, and a driver of the nation’s progress,” Jinnah Rafiq Ahmed, Executive Chairman, Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited, said.

data.title: FSSAI issues notice to Gemini Edibles over rice bran oil claims, flags Delhi’s Radisson Blu hotel
data.description:
Continuing its enforcement actions, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued a notice to Hyderabad-based Gemini Edibles & Fats India Ltd for selling rice bran oil with misleading health-benefit claims. At the same time, it issued an improvement notice to AB Hotels Ltd, which operates the Radisson Blu Hotel at Mahipalpur, New Delhi, for failing to comply with food safety and hygiene requirements. The food safety regulator said it has also suspended the licenses of two companies, DNV Foods and Jhanvitanni, for non-compliance.

Notices over misleading rice bran oil claims

In a social media post on Friday, FSSAI said it issued notices to Gemini Edibles & Fats India, Innovative Retail Concepts (BigBasket), and Flipkart India over misleading claims for the product ‘Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil’.

The regulator said the product was promoted through e-commerce platforms and social media with claims such as ‘Reduces bad cholesterol and maintains/increases good cholesterol’ and “10,000+ PPM Natural Oryzanol”.

“The cholesterol and heart-health claims were found to be not covered/permitted under the applicable claims for edible vegetable oil (rice bran oil) under the Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018,” FSSAI said. It added that the company was selling food products through its own e-commerce website without appearing to hold a valid central licence covering e-commerce activity. FSSAI directed these FBOs (food business operators) to show cause why action should not be initiated under the FSS Act, 2006.

Radisson Blu hotel faces improvement notice

Meanwhile, FSSAI issued an improvement notice to AB Hotels Ltd, which operates the Radisson Blu Hotel at Mahipalpur in New Delhi, for various non-compliances, including poor maintenance of premises and equipment, inadequate cleaning and sanitisation, stagnant water, and drainage and food-waste problems.

Deficiencies in pest control were recorded, with cockroach and fly activity observed. Food procurement and receiving checks were inadequate, including the receipt of fungal-affected and deteriorated fruits and vegetables. There were also gaps in approved-vendor records and traceability, as well as improper segregation of raw and cooked foods, vegetarian and non-vegetarian items, allergenic and non-allergenic foods, and food and non-food items, among other non-compliances. “ The FBO (AB Hotels) has been directed to take immediate corrective measures and submit a detailed action taken report with supporting documentation and photographic evidence. Failure to comply may lead to further action, including suspension of the FSSAI license,” the regulator added.

Licences suspended over food safety violations

In a separate action, FSSAI suspended the license of DNV Food Products Ltd for serious non-compliances observed during the inspection. The violations were related to hygiene, sanitation, storage and licensing. At the same time, it has also cancelled the license of Jhanvittanni for continued non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations, despite license suspension.”

data.title: PNB’s net profit rises 13% in Q2; plans to launch special campaign for RD amid bearish stock mkt
data.description:
Seeking to woo investors during ongoing stock market volatility, Punjab National Bank is launching a campaign for a special recurring deposit scheme promising assured returns. The move comes as the state-owned lender posted a record quarterly net profit of over ₹5,500 crore for Q2 FY27, shrugging off a drop in treasury income.

“We are planning to launch the RD scheme. We have the RD scheme, but we are going to popularise this now considering what is happening in the stock market,” Ashok Chandra, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Bank, told reporters in a virtual briefing which announcing the quarterly results.  Further, he said: “This is the right time to pitch this product and provide the safe return to all the customers and all the depositors.”

When asked about the less than 5 per cent growth in operating profit despite a nearly 13 per cent increase in net profit in the second quarter of the current fiscal, he said:

“This is mainly on account of lower treasury income. Last financial year, during the same period, our treasury profit was ₹1,769 crore but this quarter it is only ₹753 crore.” A shortfall of ₹1,000 crore lowered that growth rate. “If I add that, I think operating profit would have crossed more than ₹8,500 crore,” he said.

Further, he said that against the guidance of credit growth of 12-13 per cent, it is likely to be 13-14 per cent in the full year. And because of rate hike, net interest margin (NIM) could improve by 6-7 basis points during the ongoing quarter.

For the whole year, the guidance for NIM remains at 2.6-2.7 per cent. “What we are aiming that our global NIM also should cross this trajectory. Already, our domestic NIM has touched 2.74 and the global NIM is around 2.58. I am expecting that somewhere around 2.7, global NIM also should touch my end of this,” Chandra said.

On raising funds from overseas investors, Chandra said the bank will raise $1 billion under its Medium-Term Note (MTN) Programme. The bank is waiting for an opportune time to mobilise the funds, he said.

On asset quality, the bank’s gross non-performing assets (NPAs) moderated to 2.55 per cent of gross advances at the end of September 2026, down from 3.45 per cent a year ago. Similarly, net NPAs, or bad loans, fell to 0.25 per cent at the end of September 2026, down from 0.36 per cent at the end of September 2025. During the quarter, the bank has made a floating provision of ₹125 crore aggregating to ₹2,560 crore. The additional provision will help meet Expected Credit Loss (ECL) guidelines to kick in from April 1, he said, adding that the additional provision helped in improving PCR.

data.title: From Operation Sindoor to ADAS: Tonbo Imaging takes battlefield technology to civilian applications
data.description:
From countering Pakistan’s drone offensive during India’s Operation Sindoor to detecting pedestrians and cattle on dark highways and elephants along Assam’s railway corridors, military-grade imaging technology is finding potential civilian applications. Bengaluru-based Tonbo Imaging is looking to adapt its battlefield surveillance and targeting expertise for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and railway safety, opening new opportunities ahead of its ₹852-crore IPO on October 15.

Tonbo’s MGS-23 equips conventional anti-aircraft guns with thermal imaging and targeting capabilities, while it develops WaveStrike high-power microwave technology to turn off drone swarms by disrupting their electronics.

Asked about Operation Sindoor, a source familiar with Tonbo’s defence programmes declined to share operational details, citing strict military non-disclosure agreements, but said its technologies had been deployed across multiple military theatres and demonstrated operational readiness under battlefield conditions.

“We don’t make the weapon; we make the eyes and the brains of the weapon,” the source said.

FROM FIGHTER JETS TO MISSILE SEEKERS

India’s modernisation of the Su-30MKI fighter aircraft offers a potential market for Tonbo’s electro-optical and infrared technologies. Such systems help aircraft detect, identify and track targets in poor visibility, integrating with targeting pods and missile guidance systems to improve precision strikes.

Tonbo has supplied seeker-related technology for missile programmes involving Bharat Dynamics, although it has not disclosed a direct Su-30MKI integration contract.

Tonbo Imaging develops electro-optical sights, driver-vision systems, and thermal imaging payloads for precision targeting on military platforms built by partners including Larsen & Toubro (L&T) and DRDO. The Arjun Mk1A tank features a remote-controlled weapon station for its 12.7-mm machine gun, while Tonbo separately markets compact thermal weapon sights for rifles and sniper systems under its proprietary ‘Arjun’ brand.

Sources expect missile seekers to become a significant revenue driver around FY29, followed by high-power microwave systems during FY29–30. WaveStrike remains at the prototype stage.

BATTLEFIELD EYES FOR CIVILIAN ROADS

The same ability to identify heat signatures and track moving targets could help vehicles detect hazards beyond headlights.

“An elephant is one big thermal signature,” the source said, explaining that thermal imaging could alert locomotive drivers to animals crossing railway tracks, particularly along Assam’s wildlife corridors, where Tonbo is in an advanced pilot project with Indian Railways, according to sources familiar with the development.

Tonbo is exploring railway safety systems that combine thermal imaging, electro-optical sensors, and radar, alongside ADAS applications for passenger cars, commercial trucks, and mining equipment.

“The shortest-term opportunity in automotive or transportation in India is in the heavy-vehicle sector,” the source said.

“We understood two domains very well. We understood defence and we understood autonomous vehicles,” the source added.

ORDER BOOK, REVENUE AND IPO

Tonbo has a signed order book of approximately ₹290 crore, excluding defence programmes undergoing qualification and commercial negotiations, according to people familiar with its operations.

People familiar with its growth plans said revenue could cross ₹550 crore in FY27 and approach ₹1,000 crore in FY28, up from FY26 turnover of ₹362.65 crore. These estimates are not formal company guidance.

The ₹852-crore IPO is entirely an offer for sale, allowing early investors, including Celesta Capital and Edelweiss, to exit without raising fresh capital for Tonbo.

Investors including SBI Mutual Fund, Amansa, ValueQuest, 360 ONE, HDFC Life and Malabar participated in pre-IPO transactions worth approximately ₹400 crore, according to people familiar with the deals.

“Let us deliver on this business,” the source said, suggesting fresh fundraising could follow as revenue scales.

data.title: Catena Media announces preliminary Q3 results and financial target update
data.description:
Catena Media plc today publishes preliminary, unaudited results for the third quarter of 2026, together with a non-cash impairment charge and an update to the group’s 2026 financial targets.

Preliminary Q3 revenue was EUR 8.3m, down 29 percent from the same period last year (11.6m). Revenue for the first nine months was EUR 30.1m (31.0m). Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was EUR 0.7m (2.9m), including a reversal of EUR 0.7m of accruals made earlier in the year for the 2026 employee bonus programme. Adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months was EUR 4.6m (5.2m).

Given the above, the group no longer expects to reach its target of double-digit organic growth in group revenue and adjusted EBITDA in 2026.

Catena Media expects to recognise a non-cash impairment charge on intangible assets of EUR 30-35m in Q3, in accordance with IAS 36.

Several factors adversely affected operating performance in Q3. Generative search continued to transform how users discover brands online, reducing new traffic across the affiliate industry. Catena Media's traditional search rankings declined, due both to AI-assisted personalised search patterns and also to search engines continuing to elevate lower-relevancy content in search results. Certain operators also reduced their marketing budgets during the usual seasonal summer slowdown.

Since Catena Media acquires more than 90 percent of new customers under cost-per-acquisition (CPA) deals, the group has limited recurring revenue to buffer against such a combination of market pressures.

Manuel Stan, Catena Media CEO, commented: “This was a weak quarter and our results reflect that. The search landscape is undergoing a rapid and fundamental shift, and as a predominantly CPA-based business our results reflect the effects of these changes immediately and in full.

“The results reinforce the strategic direction we set out in the second quarter. We are reducing our dependence on search by diversifying our revenue streams, including through our newly announced TraffiqX project and new verticals like prediction markets, and by continuing to build the strength of our brands through investing in customer loyalty programmes. data.title: Nasdaq Pulls Back Sharply But Dow Seeing Further Upside
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Extending recent volatility on Wall Street, the major U.S. stock indexes have moved in notably opposite directions during trading on Friday.

While the tech-heavy Nasdaq has moved sharply lower, the Dow is adding to yesterday's strong gain, reaching its best intraday level in almost a month.

Currently, the Nasdaq is just off its low of the session, down 279.18 points or 1.1 percent at 26,433.85. The S&P 500 is also down 23.25 points or 0.3 percent at 7,720.81, but the Dow is up 188.62 points or 0.4 percent at 52,366.31.

Financial giant JPMorgan Chase (JPM) has helped lead the Dow higher, jumping by 2.5 percent. Home Depot (HD), American Express (AXP) and Disney (DIS) are also posting strong gains.

Meanwhile, renewed weakness among technology stocks is weighing on the Nasdaq amid concerns about debt-fueled AI infrastructure spending.

Computer hardware stocks are turning in some of the tech sector's worst performances, extending the nosedive seen over the past couple weeks, with the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index plunging by 3.2 percent.

Software, networking and semiconductor stocks are also seeing significant weakness, contributing to the slump by the Nasdaq.

Outside of the tech sector, gold stocks are seeing further upside along with the price of the precious metal, driving the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index up by 1.7 percent.

Banking, housing and utilities stocks are also seeing notable strength, possibly benefiting from a rotation out of tech stocks.

On the U.S. economic front, a report released by the Federal Reserve showed industrial production in the U.S. increased by more than expected in the month of September.

The Fed said industrial production climbed by 0.7 percent in September following a revised 0.1 percent uptick in August.

Economists had expected industrial production to rise by 0.4 percent compared to the unchanged reading originally reported for the previous month.

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly higher during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index jumped by 1.4 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index climbed by 0.5 percent.

The major European markets have also moved to the upside on the day. The German DAX Index is up by 1.1 percent, the French CAC 40 Index is up by 0.4 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index is up by 0.3 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries are seeing modest strength following yesterday's rally. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its, is down by 1.2 basis points at 5.075 percent.

data.title: Lilly’s Foundayo Pill Gets European Regulatory Backing – LLY Stock Heads For Best Week In Nearly Four Months
data.description:
Key points:
  • The EMA’s advisory committee recommended approving Foundayo for adults with obesity or those who are overweight and have related health conditions.
  • The committee also backed its use in adults with type 2 diabetes.
  • Foundayo generated $98 million in Q2 revenue.

Eli Lilly (LLY) received a boost to its European business after the European Medicines Agency’s (EMA) advisory committee recommended approval of its once-daily weight-loss pill, Foundayo, on Friday.

The recommendation comes as Lilly looks to build on the success of its blockbuster weight-loss treatments, Mounjaro and Zepbound.

LLY shares were up 1.8% at the time of writing. The stock has gained about 7.8% so far this week, heading for its best weekly gain in nearly four months.

Foundayo Moves Closer To European Launch

The EMA’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended approving Foundayo for adults with obesity or those who are overweight and have related health conditions. The committee also backed its use in adults with type 2 diabetes.

Foundayo contains Orforglipron, which helps control blood sugar and reduce appetite. Unlike some oral GLP-1 treatments, it can be taken without food or water restrictions.

The pill is already available in the U.S., the U.K. and the United Arab Emirates. In the U.S., it received FDA approval in April for weight management, while in the U.K., it received approval in August for both weight management and type 2 diabetes.

What Happens Next?

Foundayo still requires final authorization from the European Commission, which generally issues a decision within 67 days of EMA’s recommendation. While the timeline puts a potential decision around late December, Lilly has not confirmed when commercial sales would begin.

Foundayo generated $98 million in second-quarter (Q2) revenue. However, Lilly's two blockbuster drugs generated far more. In Q2, Mounjaro generated $9.94 billion in sales, up 91% year over year, while Zepbound brought in $4.93 billion, up 46%.

Retail Says LLY Is Breaking Out

Retail sentiment surrounding LLY on Stocktwits turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ over the past 24 hours, though message volumes remained ‘normal.’

One user noted that LLY stock is breaking out.

View this Stocktwits post

LLY shares have gained more than 18% so far this year, significantly outperforming rival Novo Nordisk (NVO), whose shares have slumped more than 25% over the same period.

data.title: SpaceX's spectrum deal still leaves it far from rivaling telecom giants
data.description:
Key points:
  • SpaceX agrees to buy Grain's nationwide 800 MHz portfolio for about $8 billion, a source says
  • Portfolio includes up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum and needs FCC approval
  • TD Cowen estimates nationwide terrestrial network would cost more than $80 billion

By Harshita Mary Varghese

SpaceX called its recent multibillion-dollar purchase of US airwaves a critical step towards building a mobile network, but constructing a true rival to major American carriers will require a terrestrial network and likely years of work and billions more.

Starlink became a money maker by offering internet service in rural and sparsely populated areas, where it faced little competition, as well as changing to easy-to-set-up home packages at a competitive price. Mobile will be harder.

Cities are particularly tough places for mobile telephony and are technologically challenging for mobile-to-satellite connections.

The rocket and satellite company will likely need to invest heavily in ground infrastructure, customer service, handset subsidies and promotions — costly parts of the wireless business in which AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile already have extensive operations.

Building a network would cost more than $80 billion, according to TD Cowen, and add to SpaceX's capital demands as it pours money into its Starship rocket program, AI infrastructure, and Terafab chip factory.

"It's just hard to imagine that this is all going to get done within a decade," said Julie Zhu, a research analyst at MoffettNathanson. "In the decade or so leading up to 2023, the big three spent about $650 billion in capex to build in networks that ostensibly were already finished."

Most phones have small antennas and limited transmitting power that make reliable satellite connections more challenging because satellites orbit hundreds of kilometers above Earth, much farther away than cell towers.

"There are too many pitfalls for satellite to be the only source of data," said Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy.

SPACEX PUBLISHES HYBRID SPACE-TERRESTRIAL PLAN

SpaceX has called the latest deal, in which it acquired 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain at a price a source pegged at nearly $8 billion, a "critical next step" for the nascent Starlink Mobile to provide high-speed mobile service.

"Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere," including "indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between", SpaceX said, announcing the purchase.

SpaceX has received regulatory authorization for up to 15,000 Starlink Mobile satellites and plans to deploy traditional terrestrial infrastructure such as antennas on towers and rooftops — a hybrid approach rather than pure satellite-to-phone — it laid out in a regulatory filing made public last week.

In a Starlink Mobile system, satellites could connect directly to mobile phones and indirectly by relaying signals through ground infrastructure. This is similar to the technology of a partnership between Starlink and T-Mobile, which provides the terrestrial network while Starlink supplies the satellite connectivity that fills in where there are no towers. That is a T-Mobile-branded service.

SpaceX in theory could strike a deal with one of the big three companies to use its ground infrastructure, what is known as a mobile virtual network operator, or MVNO, arrangement. However, SpaceX "appear to be going after a more build-your-own approach to a terrestrial network since nobody will offer them wholesale MVNO," Sag said.

SpaceX would need several times more spectrum to match the holdings of the three big mobile companies, although current spectrum might be enough to start. "It is for a company with zero mobile subscribers, plenty of runway, and a robust device/equipment ecosystem," TD Cowen said.

Would-be rivals dismissed the idea that the effort was an imminent threat.

T-Mobile Chief Technology Officer John Saw said SpaceX's spectrum would not be enough to match the capacity and performance of established mobile networks, while Katie Magnotta, Verizon's associate vice president of corporate communications, said, "A company can have billions of dollars of spectrum, but if they do not have the network to use it, it's just empty airwaves."

data.title: IMF Chief Says AI Is Strengthening Global Economy — But Warns Delayed Productivity Gains Could Trigger Shocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hyperscalers’ share of investment-grade bond issuance has risen more than tenfold over the past two years, according to the IMF.
  • A major cyberattack on payment and trading systems, or on access to deposits, could cause immediate losses and undermine confidence, according to Georgieva.
  • U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne argued the IMF should give greater weight to AI’s potential for positive economic shocks, Reuters reported.

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned Friday that artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger negative economic shocks if anticipated productivity gains take longer than expected, even as the technology strengthens global growth.

Speaking at an IMF-World Bank panel in Bangkok alongside Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark, Georgieva said, "If there are no safeguards, then the risks may exceed the opportunities.”

“Above all, we do need an ethical foundation, ​and I'm not sure we are there as a society," the IMF chief added.

Georgieva Calls For AI Safeguards

Georgieva advocated a combination of industry self-regulation and government involvement, including from the U.S., China and India. She highlighted access to electricity and digital infrastructure as essential to ensuring AI's benefits are widely shared.

Harvard economist Dani Rodrik also reiterated Georgieva's warning that disappointing productivity gains could result in a costly financial correction following substantial data-center investments.

IMF Flags Growing Hyperscaler Debt, Circular Financing Risks

In an IMF blog titled "The World Can't Afford to Get AI Wrong," Georgieva highlighted growing financial risks stemming from hyperscalers' increasing reliance on debt to fund AI infrastructure.

Their share of investment-grade bond issuance has increased more than tenfold in two years, rising from less than 1% to 10% and growing, according to the blog.

Georgieva also warned about circular financing arrangements in which hyperscalers invest in AI developers that subsequently purchase computing capacity from those same companies.

The IMF's October report examined 14 such transactions since 2023, identifying approximately $300 billion in equity investments and $650 billion in debt tied to $1.4 trillion in future revenue commitments.

Earnings Disappointments, Cyberattacks Could Pressure Valuations

Georgieva's blog warned that significant revenue or earnings disappointments by AI developers could undermine profitability expectations and pressure equity valuations.

A severe correction could spread through the leveraged, interconnected AI ecosystem, with losses potentially reaching global investors, the blog warned.

She also noted that AI-powered cyberattacks targeting payments, trading systems or access to bank deposits could cause immediate losses and undermine financial confidence.

However, the IMF estimated that AI could boost annual global economic growth by roughly half a percentage point over the next decade if productivity improvements materialize.

Meanwhile, Reuters reported that U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne pushed back against the IMF's emphasis on downside risks, arguing that the fund should give greater weight to AI's potential to deliver positive economic shocks.

data.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case, a close relative of other two cases
data.description:
Kenya has confirmed a third Ebola case in a close relative of the first and second cases, the health ministry said on Friday.

The ministry said in a statement that the third case was a 65-year-old woman who had been in quarantine since October 6.

"Once she developed fever, sore throat and malaise, she was isolated and specimen collected for testing. She tested positive for Ebola," the statement said, adding: "She was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care improving her chances of recovery."

Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo, which is the second-largest on record globally with more than 9,000 cases and over 4,000 deaths.

Kenya's first case emerged last week after a Kenyan man, who had been ill in Congo about a month before travelling by road to Uganda, flew to Nairobi on October 3, where a relative drove him to the hospital. He died on October 5.

data.title: World's rarest porpoise battles extinction as Mexico shrinks protected area
data.description:
Key points:
  • New agreement cuts vaquita's protected area by 86%
  • Gov't says smaller area will help fishermen
  • Only 7 to 10 vaquitas left in Gulf of California
  • Scientists hope for better enforcement to prevent extinction

By Ana Isabel Martinez and Sarah Morland

Mexico's president said on Thursday a drastic reduction in the protected area for the near-extinct vaquita marina, the world's smallest porpoise, will help fishing communities.

Critics say this week's reduction in the area where fishermen cannot use gillnets, long walls of nylon mesh, by 86% to 1,562 square kilometers (603 square miles), about the size of Greater London, threatens the survival of the species.

The prior agreement had protected an area similar to the size of the US state of Connecticut.

President Claudia Sheinbaum said the new scope aimed to protect biodiversity in the Gulf of California while also allowing fishermen to make a better living.

Authorities said the measure took into account proposals by the International Committee for the Recovery of the Vaquita, a government advisory body.

Lorenzo Rojas-Bracho, a Mexican marine biologist and leading vaquita expert who took part in the committee, said he hoped a smaller area could concentrate efforts to save the mammal.

"It is difficult to enforce a ban over a very large area, which includes vast areas with no recent records of vaquitas," Rojas-Bracho told Reuters. "If you lose a ring you don't search your entire house, you focus on where you lost it."

Scientists estimated last year there were just 7 to 10 vaquitas left, including at least one calf. The population has collapsed from around 600 in 1997, largely due to illegal fishing targeting totoaba, whose swim bladders are highly prized in Chinese medicine and can fetch up to $10,000 in Asia.

Rojas-Bracho said that if no more vaquitas are killed, the remaining handful of porpoises would have a good chance of repopulating the species.

However, he said the area needs more effective tracking of fishing boats, better monitoring and that fishermen should use alternative methods that do not put the vaquita at risk.

Gerardo Ceballos, a biologist at the National Autonomous University of Mexico, said allowing the vaquita to become extinct would amount to a moral failure.

"What's happening to the vaquita is a death foretold," he said. "We've reduced the vaquita's protected area without actually having the technical or logistical capacity to enforce regulations there; we're giving in to pressure from interested groups so a larger area can be exploited."

Ceballos said a very minimal government investment would ensure the vaquita's protection. As things currently stood, however, he believed the porpoise was on the path to extinction.

"If the vaquita goes extinct it won't solve insecurity or poverty or any of the local problems. And Mexico would lose an icon," he said. "If actions are taken, there is a possibility, a hope. And we must keep working with hope."

data.title: Technical Execution, Timing Seen Key for Quantum Computing Race — Market Talk
data.description: It's an open question as to which quantum computing company is positioned to lead a market expected to reach $10 billion in 2030, Morgan Stanley analysts write in a note. If fault-tolerant quantum computers become widely commercially adopted, that market could grow to $100 billion by 2040, they project. Still, everything hinges on technical execution and timing: each quantum company in Morgan Stanley's coverage has a milestone set for 2027, with fault-tolerant systems expected in 2029 or 2030 per company roadmaps. "Today's revenue is too small to show which businesses will succeed," the analysts write. "The investment question is which companies are most likely to reach fault tolerance first." (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
